output:
Since you didn't name the library, I used `apiclient` as a placeholder — swap it throughout. Draft is ~250 words and passes this repo's `slopwatch` ruleset clean.

---

# apiclient 2.0

apiclient 2.0 is on PyPI. Here is what changed and what the upgrade costs you.

Async is now the default. `AsyncClient` is what `apiclient.connect()` hands back; the blocking version moved to `apiclient.sync` and behaves exactly as it did in 1.x. We made the switch because most of the traffic we saw was people wrapping the sync client in a thread pool, usually with a pool size someone picked in 2021 and never revisited.

Retries moved from the client to the request. You can say `client.get(url, retries=5)` without building a second client, and the backoff policy is a plain callable you can replace.

Pagination returns an iterator. `client.list_users()` yields users and fetches pages as you consume them, instead of handing back a cursor object you had to drive yourself.

Errors have a hierarchy now: `ApiError` at the root, with `RateLimited`, `AuthError`, and `ServerError` under it. Catching the base class no longer swallows your own `TypeError`.

Three things will break. Python 3.9 support is gone. `timeout=` takes seconds rather than milliseconds, which will quietly make your timeouts 1000x longer if you skip this paragraph. `.json()` raises on an empty body instead of returning `None`.

Run `apiclient migrate .` to handle the first two mechanically. The third one needs eyes on it.

The full changelog and the migration guide are in the docs. Thanks to the 23 people who filed issues against the 2.0 betas.

---
